title: International normalized ratio (INR)

review.note: Drafted from the source below; not yet reviewed by a medical professional.

sources.title: MedlinePlus: Prothrombin Time Test and INR (PT/INR)

measures: The INR (international normalized ratio) is a standardized number based on the prothrombin time (PT) test. Using this ratio makes it easier to compare results from different labs or test methods.
context: The INR is often used to see how well a blood-thinning medicine such as warfarin is working. Alcohol, foods high in vitamin K such as green leafy vegetables, soybean and canola oils, high-fat diets, and some medicines and supplements can affect the result.
aboveRange: A higher INR means blood is taking longer than normal to form a clot, which can be associated with a higher risk of bleeding
belowRange: A lower INR means blood is clotting more easily, which can be associated with a higher risk of harmful clots
Supplements with vitamin K, or a diet high in vitamin K
